text: The Fire Keeper tends the flame at Firelink Shrine, maintaining the connection to the First Flame and allowing bonfires to function.
Ludleth of Courland is the only Lord of Cinder who willingly returned to his throne at Firelink Shrine after being resurrected.
Ludleth of Courland is frail and unable to walk or fight due to the toll of having linked the fire previously.
High Priestess Emma is an elderly steward who served Prince Lothric and the royal family.
At the Halfway Fortress on the Road of Sacrifices, the Ashen One meets Anri of Astora and the silent warrior Horace the Hushed.
Anri of Astora is also hunting the Lords of Cinder, like the Ashen One.
Anri of Astora and Horace the Hushed are specifically seeking to kill Aldrich, whom Anri calls a man-eating fiend, for his crimes.
Pontiff Sulyvahn crowned himself ruler of Irithyll of the Boreal Valley through force and cunning, wielding two enchanted greatswords imbued with fire and ghostly magic.
The Ashen One found a sword belonging to Anri of Astora among the ruins near Aldrich, suggesting Anri had tried to confront Aldrich before the Ashen One arrived.

Yhorm the Giant ruled as king over a population of humans in the Profaned Capital, genuinely loving his people and trying to protect and stabilize them despite his massive size compared to them and their fear of giants.
Before linking the flame, Yhorm the Giant gave one Storm Ruler to his trusted friend, Siegward of Catarina, with instructions to use it against him if he ever returned as a threat.
High Priestess Emma, dying at the altar in the chapel, delivered her final message to the Ashen One, urging them to make Prince Lothric become a lord and save the world.
High Priestess Emma died immediately after giving the Ashen One the Basin of Vows and her final message.
Lorian supported Prince Lothric's decision to reject the flame and followed him into isolation in the tower.
Lothric is the true target of the fight because he is the actual Lord of Cinder, while Lorian serves mainly as a weapon and distraction.
As Lothric dies, he remarks that his refusal of duty was unfair, acknowledging that he merely passed his burden to the Ashen One instead of avoiding it.
Ludleth of Courland, who had remained seated on the fifth throne throughout the story, turns to ash once the other four thrones are filled, completing the set of five Lords of Cinder.
The Firekeeper declares the Ashen One the true heir of the Lords of Cinder, not merely a substitute for them.
Slave Knight Gael approaches the Ashen One in the Cathedral of the Deep carrying a fragment of a painting that serves as a doorway to another world.
Sister Frieda (Friede) was once an Ashen One who sought to link the first flame but failed and fled into the Painted World of Ariandel instead of continuing to try.
Sister Frieda is the eldest sister of the Sable Church of Londor and is the sibling of Yuria of Londor.
Father Ariandel is a giant, corrupted crow-like guardian who sheltered Sister Frieda within the painted world.
Sister Frieda imprisons the Painter, a young girl with the power to paint new worlds, in an attic to prevent her from creating a replacement realm.
The Painter decides to name the new world she will eventually create simply "Ash."
The Painter recognizes the dark soul-veined blood as Uncle Gael's final gift to her, though she does not ask what became of him.
Nito, called the first of the dead, claimed a Lord Soul that gave him dominion over death.
The Witch of Izalith found the Soul of Life, becoming mother to the Flame Sorcerers and eventually the Daughters of Chaos.
Gwyn seized a Lord Soul of great brilliance that granted him power over lightning, becoming Lord of Sunlight.
The Furtive Pygmy found the fourth Lord Soul, the Dark Soul, a being so insignificant that history rarely mentions them.
Gwyn had three children: a firstborn son whose name was struck from history, Gwynevere, and Gwyndolin.
Gwynevere was called the Princess of Sunlight and was beloved and radiant.
Gwyndolin was born a son but raised as a daughter, possessing an affinity for the moon rather than his father's sunlight.
Gwyn commanded four legendary knights: Dragon Slayer Ornstein, Hawkeye Gough, Lord's Blade Ciaran, and Artorias of the Abyss.
Dragon Slayer Ornstein had served under Gwyn's firstborn son during the war against the dragons.
Artorias of the Abyss walked alongside a great wolf companion named Sif.
Gwyn rewarded Seath for his betrayal of the dragons by naming him a duke, giving him a fragment of his own Lord Soul, and granting him the archives to research immortality.
Seath eventually went mad in his research, creating abominations out of jealousy over scaled dragons.
After Gwyn's death, Gwynevere left Anor Londo, presumably with her husband, the flame god Flann.
Gwyndolin remained in Anor Londo, maintaining an illusion of Gwynevere's presence to keep humanity's hope and continue his father's mission of perpetuating the Age of Fire.
Dragon Slayer Ornstein eventually left Anor Londo in search of the Nameless King, Gwyn's disgraced firstborn son.
Lothric of Carim, also called Lleth, linked the flame and became a Lord of Cinder despite being a pygmy naturally aligned with darkness.
Aldrich earned the title of Lord of Cinder through sheer power despite never intending to serve the flame.
Yhorm the Giant linked the flame for a specific reason and was horrified to be awakened and asked to do it again.
Prince Lothric, called the last hope of his line, was the culmination of generations of bloodline refinement, born frail but possessing tremendous magical power.
Prince Lothric's older brother Lorian was once the kingdom's greatest champion who slew the Demon Prince.
Lorian's victory over the Demon Prince left his great sword wreathed in flame, but the demon's curse crippled his legs and left him mute, leaving him unable to walk.

Lorian chose to share his younger brother Lothric's frailty curse through magic or a soul bond so Lothric would not bear it alone, and the two became inseparable, with Lorian carrying Lothric on his back while Lothric guided him with magic and strategy.
The Ashen One is one such Unkindled, awakening in the Cemetery of Ash where they previously failed and died in a past age.
Lothric of Carim is the only Lord of Cinder who sits willingly on his throne at Firelink Shrine without being hunted down.
Lothric of Carim has had his legs cut off, possibly as punishment, sacrifice, or to prevent him from walking away like the other Lords of Cinder.
Lothric of Carim genuinely believes the Age of Fire must continue and fears the darkness and hollowing that would follow its end.
Upon being raised again as a Lord of Cinder, Yhorm returned to his own throne room in the ruined Profaned Capital rather than Firelink Shrine, waiting for Siegward to fulfill his promise and end him.
Aldrich was originally a cleric who developed a taste for human flesh, becoming a bloated mass of sludge and darkness after consuming many people.
Aldrich believed an Age of the Deep Sea was coming and decided to accelerate its arrival by devouring gods to hasten the end of the Age of Fire.
Pontiff Sulyvahn was born in the Painted World of Ariandel, a realm accessible only through a scrap of canvas, meant to be a gentle refuge.
Sulyvahn's sorcery description states he had little use for his frigid homeland since he had not yet experienced loss, suggesting an innate coldness.
As a young sorcerer, Sulyvahn left the Painted World and discovered the Profaned Capital and its unfading Profaned Flame, which ignited a burning ambition in him.
Sulyvahn traveled to Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, a once-glorious city of moon-worshipping sorcerers connected to Gwyndolin and the old gods.
Prince Lothric and Prince Lorian are called the Twin Princes, though they are not literal twins.
Lorian is the elder brother and was once the kingdom's greatest warrior, while Lothric is the younger, frail prince born to link the flame.
Lothric was educated by the finest scholars in the Grand Archives, possibly including Pontiff Sulyvahn, who taught him doubts about the necessity of linking the flame.
The Painted World of Ariandel is ruled by Father Ariandel, who flagellates himself to maintain the painting, and Sister Friede, who wields a scythe and claims to protect the painting.
Slave Knight Gael brings the Ashen One to the Painted World and introduces them to the Painter, a girl who needs fire, the dark soul of man as pigment, and help to create a new painting.

In the Ashen Wasteland, Slave Knight Gael is found covered in blood among the desiccated Pygmy Lords, having drunk their dried blood in a mad attempt to gather fragments of the dark soul for the Painter's pigment.
Slave Knight Gael never aspired to be a hero and knew he wasn't strong enough to save the world, but tried anyway because someone he cared about needed help.
Slave Knight Gael's journey took him through vast ages and impossible battles, all the way to the end of time itself.
In the end, Slave Knight Gael was corrupted and transformed into the very type of monster he had fought for so long to prevent.
Because of Slave Knight Gael's persistence through madness and corruption, the painter received the pigment she needed.
